config.title: ::placeholder and ::selection

intro.title: ::placeholder and ::selection
intro.body: In this lesson, you will style the placeholder text inside input fields and the selected text on a webpage using CSS pseudo-elements. You will build a simple form with an input field and a paragraph to practice applying custom colors, backgrounds, and fonts to these elements. The core concept is using ::placeholder to style temporary input hints and ::selection to style highlighted text. You will work with basic CSS properties like color, background-color, and font-family. By the end, you'll know how to enhance form usability and visual feedback with these selectors.
intro.usecase: The ::placeholder and ::selection pseudo-elements are essential for enhancing user experience in interactive web applications. Developers use ::placeholder to style form input hints in login screens, search bars, and checkout forms—making them more readable and visually integrated with the overall design. The ::selection styling is commonly applied in content-rich interfaces like documentation sites, blog platforms, and dashboards to customize how highlighted text appears, improving readability and brand consistency. These selectors help create polished, accessible interfaces where visual feedback matters, from data-heavy admin panels to public-facing contact forms.

objectives: Apply the ::placeholder pseudo-element to style placeholder text in form inputs
Configure the ::selection pseudo-element to customize text selection appearance
Implement both ::placeholder and ::selection styles in a single CSS rule set
Manipulate color, background, and font properties for placeholder styling
Control text selection appearance using background-color and color properties
Construct CSS rules that target specific input types with ::placeholder
Update existing form styles to include custom placeholder and selection effects

steps.title: Set up the HTML structure for styling
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a basic structure including a text input field and a paragraph of text that we can style with CSS pseudo-elements.
steps.hint: Start with the standard HTML5 doctype and include a head section with a title, then add a body with an input and a paragraph.
steps.analogousExample: Select some text in this paragraph to see ::selection styling.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Pseudo-elements Demo</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add an input field with a placeholder and a paragraph with selectable text here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: A valid HTML file with an input field containing placeholder text and a paragraph with selectable text, ready for CSS styling.
successCriteria: The HTML file includes a text input with a placeholder attribute and a paragraph element with text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both an input field with a placeholder attribute and a paragraph with text content.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a complete HTML file with both an input element (with placeholder) and a paragraph element.

    <style>
      /* Add your CSS rules here */
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add an input field with a placeholder and a paragraph with selectable text here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: A <style> element is added to the HTML document, ready for CSS rules.
successCriteria: The <head> section contains a <style> element with opening and closing tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the <style> element is properly placed inside the <head> section with both opening and closing tags.

steps.title: Add more placeholder styling properties
steps.instruction: In the existing ::placeholder rule, add two new properties: set font-weight to bold and background-color to lightyellow.
steps.hint: Add 'font-weight: bold;' and 'background-color: lightyellow;' inside the existing ::placeholder selector block.
steps.seedCode:

<html lang="en">

<body>
    <!-- Add an input field with a placeholder and a paragraph with selectable text here -->

steps.expectedOutcome: The ::placeholder rule now includes four properties: color, font-style, font-weight, and background-color.
successCriteria: The ::placeholder selector contains 'font-weight: bold;' and 'background-color: lightyellow;' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styling, but make sure to include both 'font-weight: bold;' and 'background-color: lightyellow;' inside the ::placeholder rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ::placeholder rule should include 'font-weight: bold;' and 'background-color: lightyellow;' in addition to the existing properties.

steps.title: Introduce the ::selection pseudo-element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the ::selection pseudo-element inside the <style> tag to target user-selected text.
steps.hint: The ::selection pseudo-element allows you to style text that the user selects with their mouse or keyboard. Start by writing ::selection { }.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Pseudo-elements Demo</title>
    <style>
      /* Add your CSS rules here */
      ::placeholder {
        color: gray;
        font-style: italic;
        /* Add font-weight and background-color here */
      }
      /* Add ::selection rule here */
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add an input field with a placeholder and a paragraph with selectable text here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file now contains a rule for the ::selection pseudo-element, ready for styling properties to be added in the next step.
successCriteria: A ::selector { } rule is added inside the <style> tag.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a rule starting with ::selection { } inside the <style> tag.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ::selection rule is missing. Add ::selection { } inside the <style> tag to target selected text.

steps.title: Add more selection styling properties
steps.instruction: Extend the existing ::selection rule to include a text-shadow property and a cursor property.
steps.hint: Add the text-shadow and cursor properties inside the existing ::selection rule. For text-shadow, you can use values like '2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.5)'. For cursor, try 'text'.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Pseudo-elements Demo</title>
    <style>
      /* Add your CSS rules here */
      ::placeholder {
        color: gray;
        font-style: italic;
        /* Add font-weight and background-color here */
      }
      ::selection {
        background-color: yellow;
        color: black;
        /* Add text-shadow and cursor properties here */
      }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add an input field with a placeholder and a paragraph with selectable text here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The ::selection rule will have text-shadow and cursor properties added to enhance the styling of selected text.
successCriteria: The ::selection rule includes both text-shadow and cursor properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added one of the required properties. Make sure to include both text-shadow and cursor inside the ::selection rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ::selection rule should contain both text-shadow and cursor properties. Check that you've added them correctly inside the rule.

steps.title: Review browser compatibility considerations
steps.instruction: Add a CSS comment below your existing styles explaining browser compatibility considerations for ::placeholder and ::selection, including vendor prefixes for older browsers.
steps.hint: Use a CSS comment (/* ... */) to add notes about browser support. Mention that ::placeholder may need -webkit- and -moz- prefixes for older browsers, while ::selection is widely supported but may need -moz- prefix for Firefox.
steps.analogousExample: /* Browser compatibility: For ::placeholder, add -webkit- and -moz- prefixes for older browsers. Example: input::-webkit-input-placeholder { color: gray; } */
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Pseudo-elements Demo</title>
    <style>
      /* Add your CSS rules here */
      ::placeholder {
        color: gray;
        font-style: italic;
        /* Add font-weight and background-color here */
      }
      ::selection {
        background-color: yellow;
        color: black;
        /* Add text-shadow and cursor properties here */
      }
      /* Add browser compatibility comment here */
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add an input field with a placeholder and a paragraph with selectable text here -->
    
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS comment is added explaining browser compatibility and vendor prefixes for ::placeholder and ::selection pseudo-elements.
successCriteria: The CSS comment includes mentions of vendor prefixes (-webkit-, -moz-) and browser support considerations for both pseudo-elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a comment, but it should specifically mention vendor prefixes (-webkit-, -moz-) and browser support for ::placeholder and ::selection.
steps.feedbackWrong: The comment doesn't address browser compatibility or vendor prefixes. Review the hint and try again.
